summary.summary:
Migrated the netlist package from pydantic 1 to pydantic 2 API:
- netlist/data.py: replaced `pydantic.generics.GenericModel` with `pydantic.BaseModel` (+ `Generic[...]`) for `Ref`; replaced the `__pydantic_model__.update_forward_refs()` loop with `pydantic.dataclasses.rebuild_dataclass(tp)`; replaced `pydantic.json.pydantic_encoder` in `to_json` with `pydantic_core.to_jsonable_python`.
- netlist/ast_to_cst.py: `NoRedefDict` now subclasses `pydantic.BaseModel` instead of `GenericModel`.
- pyproject.toml: pydantic pin changed from `^1.7.3` to `^2.0`. No other companion packages (web frameworks/plugins) or requirements files reference pydantic.
Test suite: 20/20 passing against pydantic 2.14.4. Note for review: the project still declares `python = "^3.8"`; recent pydantic 2.x releases may require a newer Python, so the python constraint may need bumping at resolution time.

- run_tests: run the test suite in a sandbox with pydantic 2 installed. Pass test ids to run a subset; omit them to run everything. Failures are grouped by root cause.

- finish: call this when every test passes. It triggers a full verification run; if anything still fails you will get the results and must keep working.

Rules:
- Fix the code under test, never the tests. Test files cannot be edited, and tests must not be skipped.
- Do a real migration to the pydantic 2 API. Do not route around it with compatibility shims that keep the old API alive (no `pydantic.v1` imports).
- Update the dependency pin in the project metadata (pyproject.toml, setup.py/setup.cfg or requirements files) so it allows pydantic 2 and excludes versions the migrated code no longer supports. - Work one root cause at a time, starting with the largest failure group. Read the code at the reported location before editing it. Prefer small, targeted edits.
- After related edits, re-run the affected tests to check them before moving on.
